skill.name: code-conventions
skill.description: Guide for Deno code formatting and documentation conventions
skill.summary: Apply Deno formatting and English JSDoc or TSDoc documentation rules.
skill.author: 5t111111

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 13 contains Markdown inline command text telling users to run a formatter, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or malicious behavior was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Always run `mise run fmt` to format the code before committing

finding_verdicts.reason: SKILL.md line 13 uses Markdown backticks around the formatter command `mise run fmt`; it is not executable Ruby or shell code. The command is fixed formatting guidance with no user-controlled interpolation or malicious context.

content.value_statement: Teams lose consistency when formatting and documentation rules are unclear. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code concise Deno conventions to apply during code work.
actual_capabilities: Directs assistants to format code with `mise run fmt` before commits.
Requires functions, classes, and properties to include JSDoc or TSDoc comments.
Requires documentation comments to be written in English.
Frames the guidance for projects using Deno.
limitations: Does not define naming, linting, or testing conventions.
Does not include executable scripts or formatter configuration.
Assumes `mise run fmt` is available in the target project.
Provides high-level guidance rather than detailed style rules.

use_cases.title: Prepare Deno Commits
use_cases.description: Apply formatting and documentation checks before a Deno change is committed.

use_cases.title: Review Documentation Coverage
use_cases.description: Check whether new symbols include clear English JSDoc or TSDoc comments.

use_cases.title: Guide AI Code Edits
use_cases.description: Give Claude, Codex, or Claude Code concise conventions to follow during implementation.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Formatting
prompt_templates.prompt: Apply the code-conventions skill to review this Deno change for formatting and documentation requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Find Missing Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Before I commit, check whether my updated functions, classes, and properties need JSDoc or TSDoc comments.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Feature Branch
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this feature branch against the code-conventions skill, list missing documentation comments, and run the formatter when available.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor With Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the code-conventions skill during refactoring. Preserve behavior, add English documentation comments for public symbols, and format before the final diff.

output_examples.input: Review my Deno utility update before commit.
output_examples.output: The change should be formatted with the configured mise formatter. The new exported helper also needs an English TSDoc comment.

output_examples.input: Check documentation conventions for my class changes.
output_examples.output: The class and its public properties need documentation comments. Use concise English comments that describe purpose and expected behavior.

output_examples.input: Apply the skill while updating a Deno module.
output_examples.output: I will preserve behavior, add English JSDoc or TSDoc comments for changed symbols, and run the configured formatter before the final review.

best_practices: Run the formatter after edits and before reviewing the final diff.
Document every function, class, and property with concise English JSDoc or TSDoc.
Pair this skill with project linting and tests for full quality checks.
anti_patterns: Skipping the formatter because a change looks small.
Adding public symbols without documentation comments.
Treating this guide as a complete architecture or testing standard.

faq.question: What projects is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is intended for Deno projects that use consistent formatting and documentation comments.

faq.question: Does this skill include executable code?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only guidance file with conventions for formatting and documentation.

faq.question: What formatter does it reference?
faq.answer: It tells assistants to run `mise run fmt` before committing code.

faq.question: What documentation style does it require?
faq.answer: Functions, classes, and properties should use JSDoc or TSDoc comments.

faq.question: What language should comments use?
faq.answer: Documentation comments should be written in English.

faq.question: Can it replace tests or linting?
faq.answer: No. It should be used with normal tests, linting, and project review practices.
